all_quotes.quote: In both methods, $\Delta\!R$ increases with both $L\!B$ and HPBW. However, $\Delta\!R$ is larger when the half-power method is used, being less pronounced for narrow HPBW and more pronounced for wider HPBW.
For the first time, limb brightening values for frequencies of 212 and 405 GHz were estimated.

The limb brightening determination from solar scan simulations yields ranges of $L\!B$ that agree with previous measurements (cite: selhor19) and is able to estimate $L\!B$ from low spatial resolution solar maps such as those from SST.

Since observation at distinct wavelengths probe different layers of the solar atmosphere, the study of the solar radius and limb brightening provides important information about the solar atmosphere structure and temperature.

Since structural antenna deformations change the expected size and form of the beams (cite: valle21), in this study we only use receivers #3 (212 GHz) and #5 (405 GHz), which beams have less deformation compared to the other ones.
